files_by_author_class.note: A concept is a set of kinds of author with every file that all of them touched. 'support' counts the files touched by at least those kinds; 'exact' counts the files touched by exactly those kinds and no other.

repos_by_author_class.reads: every own commit that is not a merge: mass edits and commits with no paths included, private commits as counts
repos_by_author_class.objects: repos with at least one own commit that is not a merge
repos_by_author_class.attributes: the identity classes of their authors
repos_by_author_class.note: Private repos enter with counts only. first_commit_by_class names one commit per class as its witness.

areas.reads: usable commits: public, not merges, with paths, at most 15 files
areas.attributes: the areas (repo/top-level folder) they touch; areas with fewer than 3 commits dropped
areas.note: A rule 'a => b' reads: of the commits that touched a, this share also touched b. 'exceptions' are the commits that touched a but not b. Only rules with confidence at least 0.8 are kept.

method.betweenness: Brandes, exact (fractions), on weighted distances for files and hop counts for the session and author graphs
method.passage points: a node whose removal disconnects two repos that were connected (Callon)

files.reads: usable commits: public, not merges, with paths, at most 15 files

jaccard.distance: 1 / Jaccard (commits that changed both over commits that changed either), high-churn files set aside

files.note: Two files are linked when one commit changed both. Betweenness counts the shortest paths between other files that pass through a file; 'share' is that count over the pairs of other files in its component, so compare files within one component. A cut vertex is a file whose removal splits its component. The count variant ranks files that change often (READMEs, build files) first; the Jaccard variant sets aside 12 high-churn files and normalises by how often each file changes.

sessions.reads: every own commit that carries a Claude-Session trailer: merges and mass edits included, private commits as counts
sessions.note: One Claude session that committed to two repos links them directly (repo_pairs); two repos joined only through a chain of sessions and other repos are linked through others; two repos no chain joins are in no_recorded_link. Only commits that carry a Claude-Session trailer can show a link, so that is 'no recorded session link', not 'no link', and the repos may still be tied in other ways. A passage point between two repos is a node every path between them in this session graph crosses. Private repos enter with commit counts only.

authors.reads: every own commit that is not a merge: mass edits and commits with no paths included, private commits as counts
authors.note: Identity labels from the family config, not people's names or addresses. With few identities this graph is mostly two hubs; a repo with one author hangs off that author.

questions: Which recorded sessions connect these repositories?

pipeline.does: Reads every repo's history on all refs and its tip tree. Emails never leave this module; Claude-Session URLs become short hashes; a private repo keeps only times, identity classes and sizes.

Finds ties between repos: written commit hashes (pins), names in manifests, imports, CI, code and docs, identical files, one Claude session committing to two repos, forks, the second account and the stated lineage. Grades C, L or S by rule.

Formal concept analysis, three ways: files by the kinds of author that touched them (a lattice), repos by the kinds of author they have seen, and commits by the areas they touch (rules that name their exceptions). Mass edits, merges and private commits are set aside and counted. Its own check re-derives every witness and count from the commits, apart from the lattice code, and fails the stage if one does not hold.

traps: A few mass edits (generated runs, assets, sweeps) carry most file touches; a commit of more than 15 files is set aside and counted, or every file it touched would look coupled to every other.
Exact implications are too strict for real repos, so area rules are kept at 80% confidence or more and every rule lists the commits that break it.
method.reads: how_built stage concepts; the concepts tool answers lookups

pipeline.does: Betweenness, cut vertices and passage points on three graphs: files that change in the same commit (two distances), Claude sessions by repo, and authors by repo. Exact arithmetic (fractions), so tied paths are real ties. Its own check recounts the session and author graphs by brute force, and the file graphs' sizes, clusters, cut vertices and which files lie on a shortest path.

traps: Hub files (READMEs, build files) top raw betweenness because they change with everything; the Jaccard variant sets the high-churn files aside and normalises by how often each file changes. Both are kept.
Betweenness is not the same as a passage point: a passage point is a node every path between two groups must cross.
The session graph only sees commits that carry a Claude-Session trailer: two repos no chain of sessions joins have no recorded session link, not no link, and the ties may still join them.
Each part says what it read: the file graph reads usable commits only, the session graph every commit with a Claude-Session trailer, the author graph every commit but merges.
method.reads: how_built stage bridges; the bridges tool answers lookups

pipeline.does: Imports the fork masterclass's hand-graded ties and the fork's commit series, with addresses scrubbed.

Data audit, robust distribution profiles under four declared forks, rhythm facts, rule-based outlier flags, and a declared battery of 12 looks (6 contrasts between two author classes, 6 drifts within one) with a seeded permutation null, Benjamini-Hochberg q and a Confirmed/Likely/Suspected robustness grade. Integer arithmetic only; an independent check re-derives every number.
Computes the signals: totals, shares, rhythm, outliers, hotspots, pins. Each signal's sentence is built by code from its own numbers.

pipeline.model: Claude wrote the spec's prose (view captions, tour stops, suggested questions) in a Claude Code session. The prose holds no numbers of its own: every number is a {signal.path} slot that code fills from the profile, and the fact gate fails the build on a digit outside a slot or a slot that does not resolve.
pipeline.does: Checks the spec against its schema and the profile, and fills its slots.

inputs: the tool's own source and git

pipeline.does: Writes one X3D 4.0 scene: the time helix, the tie constellation, the code city, the concept lattice, the bridges, and the tool's own pipeline, with viewpoints for the tour.
Projects witnessed ties into conservative typed relation records, then assembles the Artifact folder: vendored X_ITE, the label font, the scene, the data bundle and the page code.

XSD, the Loom gate with the fork validator, the fact gate (no digit outside a slot, every claim backed), the privacy gate, the witness gate (no tie without evidence; the concepts, bridges and eda sections recomputed and re-derived from the commits), the scene gate (independent static constellation geometry, source witnesses and grade encoding), the tool gate (every tool runs under 32 KB, aliases resolve, unknown names are refused, the MCP server answers), and a live X_ITE run under a strict content policy in which Ask runs against a stand-in for the sample runtime.
sha256 of every input, module, output and gate result, and one digest over them.

limits: Static scene verification covers the declared constellation glyphs and polylines and the look gallery (each panel, bar, cube and text against the stored looks); other geometry, visibility, animation and rendered pixels require separate checks.
Typed traversal follows the direction and grade of recorded predicates. Static references and configured use do not establish runtime execution or causation.
A private repo shows only commit times, identity classes and sizes: no subjects, paths, branches or files.
People appear as identity labels from the family config; an identity the config does not name counts as an upstream contributor.
Lines changed come from git numstat, so a vendored schema or a generated file counts as much as hand-written code.
The masterclass ties were graded on the date their source records; some repos have moved since (see curated.notes).
Commits made after the harvest are not in the data, including this tool's own later commits.
Concepts and bridges read file paths from git numstat without following renames, so a renamed file counts as two files.

The file lattice, the area rules and the file co-change graph set aside merges, private commits and commits of more than 15 files; the repo lattice and the author graph leave out only merges, and the session graph reads every commit with a Claude-Session trailer. Each answer counts what its part set aside.

Contrast grades are robustness checks over declared variations (four forks, counted once when they hold the same commits, leave-one-repo-out, repo strata, interleaved-week halves), not probabilities; commits are treated as exchangeable and the multiplicity correction assumes independent or positively dependent looks.
Times are UTC author times with no recorded offset; the quiet window and burst counts are descriptive and do not locate a timezone.
Slice profiles asked through the eda tool are descriptive and ungraded; only the 12 declared looks and the flag rules carry grades.

claude_in_the_data.note: The Claude answering in this page is not the session that wrote these commits and has no memory of them. It knows them only from this data: commit times, sizes, subjects, trailers and session hashes.

denominators.note: Commits only count authorship. Commits under HagopJay's names with a Claude co-author trailer count as his; squashed or rebased history hides work either way.

busiest_month.code:
# Busiest month
    per_month = collections.Counter(_day(c["t"])[:7] for _, c in own)
    month, month_n = max(per_month.items(), key=lambda kv: (kv[1], kv[0])) if per_month else (None, 0)
    if month:
        y, m = int(month[:4]), int(month[5:])
        month_end = (dt.date(y + (m == 12), m % 12 + 1, 1) - dt.timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()
        month_name = dt.date(y, m, 1).strftime("%B %Y")
    else:
        month_end = month_name = None
    sig(
        "busiest_month", "time",
        (f"{month_n} of the {total} commits ({_pct(month_n, total)}%) have author timestamps in {month_name}, the busiest month."
         if month else "No own commits were observed; a busiest month is unavailable."),
        month=month, month_name=month_name, commits=month_n, total=total, share=_pct(month_n, total) if total else None,
        **{"from": month + "-01" if month else None, "to": month_end}, by_month=dict(sorted(per_month.items())),
        available=bool(per_month),
    )

busiest_day.code:
# Busiest day
    per_day = collections.Counter(_day(c["t"]) for _, c in own)
    peak_day, peak_n = max(per_day.items(), key=lambda kv: (kv[1], kv[0])) if per_day else (None, 0)
    peak_repos = collections.Counter(n for n, c in own if _day(c["t"]) == peak_day)
    sig(
        "busiest_day", "time",
        (f"The busiest day was {_human_date(peak_day)}: {peak_n} commits in {len(peak_repos)} repos, "
         f"led by {peak_repos.most_common(1)[0][0]} ({peak_repos.most_common(1)[0][1]})." if peak_day else
         "No own commits were observed; a busiest day is unavailable."),
        day=peak_day, commits=peak_n, repos=dict(peak_repos),
        top_repo=peak_repos.most_common(1)[0][0] if peak_repos else None,
        top_commits=peak_repos.most_common(1)[0][1] if peak_repos else 0,
        second_repo=(peak_repos.most_common(2)[1][0] if len(peak_repos) > 1 else None),
        second_commits=(peak_repos.most_common(2)[1][1] if len(peak_repos) > 1 else 0),
    )

ai_share_by_repo.code:
# AI share by repo
    ai_by_repo = {}
    for r in repos:
        oc = [c for c in r.get("commits", []) if not c.get("upstream")]
        if len(oc) >= 5:
            ai_by_repo[r["name"]] = (_pct(sum(1 for c in oc if c["cls"] == "ai"), len(oc)), len(oc))
    hi = max(ai_by_repo.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1][0]) if ai_by_repo else None
    lo = min(ai_by_repo.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1][0]) if ai_by_repo else None
    sig(
        "ai_share_by_repo", "identity",
        (f"Claude's share of commits runs from {lo[1][0]}% in {lo[0]} to {hi[1][0]}% in {hi[0]}." if ai_by_repo else
         "No repo has at least five own commits; the between-repo share comparison is unavailable."),
        shares={k: v[0] for k, v in ai_by_repo.items()}, commits={k: v[1] for k, v in ai_by_repo.items()},
        available=bool(ai_by_repo), minimum_commits=5,

weekly_mix.code:
# Weekly AI share across the family (ISO weeks with at least 5 commits)
    weeks = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
    for _, c in own:
        y, w, _ = _d(c["t"]).isocalendar()
        weeks[f"{y}-W{w:02d}"][c["cls"]] += 1
    wk = [(k, v) for k, v in sorted(weeks.items()) if sum(v.values()) >= 5]
    sig(
        "weekly_mix", "identity",
        ("Week by week, Claude's share of commits: " + ", ".join(f"{k} {_pct(v['ai'], sum(v.values()))}% of {sum(v.values())}" for k, v in wk) + "."
         if wk else "No week has at least five own commits; the weekly comparison is unavailable."),
        weeks={k: dict(v) for k, v in wk},
        available=bool(wk), minimum_commits=5,
    )

                                                (merges, "merges"), (privc, "private commits"), (nopath, "public commits with no paths")) if n]

        n_b, n_g = len(brid), len(big)                        # a repo can have a cluster of ten in which no file lies between two
        n_hc = len(bridges["files"]["high_churn"])
        rows = bridge_rows(hubs, brid)

        hub_lead = list(hubs.items())[:1]
        if brid:
            body = ((("the one repo" if n_g == 1 else f"all {n_g} repos") if n_b == n_g else f"{n_b} of the {n_g} repos")
                    + f" with a cluster of ten or more files {'has' if n_b == 1 else 'have'} a file between others in it; "
                    + "; ".join(f"in {r}, {_short(v['file'])} is on {v['share_pct']}% of the shortest paths between the other files of its "
                                f"cluster of {v['cluster']}" for r, v in lead) + ".")
        elif n_g:
            body = ("the one repo with a cluster of ten or more files has no file between others in it." if n_g == 1
                    else f"none of the {n_g} repos with a cluster of ten or more files has a file between others in it.")
        else:

            + ((" With them kept, hubs such as " if n_hc else " Counting shared commits instead, hubs such as ")

            rows=len(rows[:BRIDGE_ROWS]), rows_max=BRIDGE_ROWS, rows_left_out=rows[BRIDGE_ROWS:],

size = next((r for r in eda["profile"]["records"]
                     if r["slice"] == "family" and r["fork"] == "no_merge" and r["measure"] == "lines"), None)
        rules = eda["flags"]["by_rule"]
        fcount = {g: sum(r["counts"][g] for r in rules.values()) for g in "CLS"}
        if size is None or not size["available"]:
            # One sig() call per id, so how_built's signal_code shows the whole computation, not an early exit.
            text = "Commit size could not be profiled: fewer than 10 commits outside merges."
            vals = dict(available=False, reason=(size or {}).get("reason") or "fewer than 10 commits outside merges")
        else:
            gini = stats.decimal_str(size["gini_permille"], 1000, 3) if size["gini_permille"] is not None else "n/a"
            text = (f"Commit size outside merges: median {size['p50']} lines changed, 90th percentile {size['p90']}, largest {size['max']} "
                    f"(Gini {gini}); {sum(fcount.values())} flags on commits for being unusually large or following a long quiet spell: "
                    f"{fcount['C']} Confirmed, {fcount['L']} Likely, {fcount['S']} Suspected.")
            vals = dict(available=True, n=size["n"], p50=size["p50"], p90=size["p90"], p99=size["p99"], max=size["max"],
                        gini_permille=size["gini_permille"], flagged=sum(fcount.values()), confirmed=fcount["C"], likely=fcount["L"],
                        suspected=fcount["S"])
        sig("eda_profile", "outlier", text, **vals, from_stage="eda")

            top = eda_top_finding(looks["findings"])
            text = (f"{led['declared']} declared looks ({n_contrast} contrasts between {lab[looks['pair'][0]]} and "
                    f"{lab[looks['pair'][1]]}, {n_drift} drifts within one class): "
                    f"{led['by_grade']['C']} Confirmed, {led['by_grade']['L']} Likely, {led['by_grade']['S']} Suspected, "
                    f"{ungraded} without a grade, {led['not_run']} not run. "
                    f"Grades are robustness checks over {n_forks} declared forks ({n_distinct} distinct here), not probabilities.")
            vals = dict(available=True, declared=led["declared"], contrasts=n_contrast, drifts=n_drift,
                        confirmed=led["by_grade"]["C"], likely=led["by_grade"]["L"], suspected=led["by_grade"]["S"],
                        without_grade=ungraded, not_run=led["not_run"], forks=n_forks, distinct_forks=n_distinct,
                        **({"top_id": top} if top else {}))
        sig("eda_findings", "identity", text, **vals, from_stage="eda")

limitations.text: Times are author times in UTC; the harvest records no timezone offset, so local hours are unknown.
Renames are not followed: a moved file counts as a deletion and an addition, and per-file history stops at the move.
0 commits flagged as upstream are dropped before any statistic; only the family's own commits are described.
Private repos contribute counts, sizes and times only: no sha, subject, path or kind list reaches this file.
Contrasts treat commits as exchangeable under the null; commits of one session or day are correlated, so permutation scores are anti-conservative.

audit.scope: Checks run over the family's own non-upstream commits as bundled. Grade C is a contradiction of the harvest's own contract, L a likely defect, S a suspicion; none says which side is wrong. Witnesses are public 12-hex shas only; private repos contribute counts.

profile.scope: Descriptive only: no test, no grade. Author times in UTC; the first member of a slice has no gap. A slice with fewer than 10 commits in a fork is unavailable, not zero. Private repos enter with their counts, sizes and times.

measure_defs.gap_s: seconds since the previous member of the slice, ordered by (t,i); the first member has none

quiet.threshold: an hour is quiet when it holds at most a quarter of the uniform expectation (96 * hour count <= n); hours are UTC author-time hours; the window is the longest circular run of quiet hours; descriptive and ungraded

rhythm.scope: Descriptive, ungraded, UTC author time. Built on non-merge commits; a slice below 20 commits has no bursts and below 120 no quiet window. No dates are stored.

concentration.scope: all files at the pinned tip with default-branch non-merge history; renames not followed; vendored and generated files count in full

flags.scope: Commit indices only. A flag says a commit is atypical for its stratum in k of m distinct forks where it could be evaluated (forks holding the same commits count once); it says nothing about the commit being wrong. Lists are capped; counts are exact.

size_high.definition: log2 bin of add+del is at least max(3, 3 MAD) above the stratum's lower median and the commit changes at least 64 lines

gap_long.definition: the commit ends a gap whose log2 minute bin is at least max(4, 3 MAD) above the repo's lower median and the gap is at least 604800 seconds

ledger.bh_note: BH assumes independent or positively dependent looks; looks here share commits, so q is indicative

looks.grade_rule: A look is graded by the first rule that matches: not run or effect below the floor (|Cliff's delta| 147/1000, total variation 1/10) or add-one count above 1/20 gives no grade; q above 1/10 or an opposite effect in a repo gives Suspected; otherwise Likely unless q is at most 1/20, at least one repo holds 20 commits of each group, the interleaved-week halves replicate and at least 3 distinct forks (forks holding exactly the same commits count once) and 3 leave-one-repo-out runs are evaluable and all agree, which gives Confirmed. A robustness grade over declared checks, not a likelihood or a chance estimate; Confirmed does not mean causal or predictive.

say_at_most.C: a pattern that survived every declared check in this history; not causal, not predictive
say_at_most.L: a likely pattern in this history; at least one robustness check failed or could not be run
say_at_most.S: worth a second look; do not call it real

looks.scope: the recorded commits of this family; commits are treated as exchangeable under the null; not a population and not a cause
